title: Proposition 4 and Theorem 2 in Doe and Roe (2025)
headline: Proposition 4 is false as printed (an application). Theorem 2, the main result, is not affected; a deep audit found no defect in it.

work.title: Monotone Allocation Rules in Finite Contests

claims.label: Proposition 4
claims.statement: In every two-prize contest with n ≥ 3 contestants, the rank-order rule is the unique allocation rule that is monotone, anonymous and budget-balanced.
claims.quantifiers: for every n ≥ 3; uniqueness among monotone, anonymous, budget-balanced rules

result.witness: For n = 3 and prize vector (1, ½), a second rule satisfies every stated condition. The full allocation table is in the evidence package.
result.repair_note: Requiring strict monotonicity restores uniqueness in all cases checked.
not_claimed: Theorem 2, the paper's main characterization, is not refuted.
The proposition is not claimed to fail for n = 2.

The researcher verified the example with separately written code in exact rational arithmetic.

claims.label: Theorem 2
claims.statement: A monotone, anonymous allocation rule on a finite contest is implementable by single-crossing payments.
claims.quantifiers: for every finite contest and every monotone, anonymous rule

result.search_scope: All monotone, anonymous rules for n = 2 to 5 on a seven-point type grid; the proof read line by line.
result.limits: Infinite type spaces are covered by the proof reading only.
